blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

items.t: Nearest rapid-transit station: Mission City Station (West Coast Express), 33200 North Railway Ave, Mission, southwest of this area.
No FVRD-administered BC Transit route is routed to Durieu: the FVRD administers Route 71 Agassiz-Harrison, Route 72 Hope and Route 66 Fraser Valley Express only.
Cascade Falls Regional Park, 36421 Ridgeview Road, Deroche: 22-hectare FVRD park in Electoral Area F northeast of Mission, 30-metre waterfall, 1 km trail.
Mission Library, 33247 Second Avenue, Mission.
No school in Durieu itself is listed for SD75; the schools below are outside Durieu, in Dewdney and Mission; confirm the catchment with the district.
Dewdney Elementary, K-6, SD75, 37151 Hawkins-pickle Rd B107, Dewdney; confirm the catchment with the district.
Hatzic Elementary, K-6, SD75, 8465 Draper St, Mission; confirm the catchment with the district.
Hatzic Middle School, 7-9, SD75, 34875 Moffat Avenue, Mission; confirm the catchment with the district.
Mission Senior Secondary, 10-12, SD75, 32939 7th Ave, Mission; confirm the catchment with the district.

Official boundary: no official boundary for the Durieu sub-area was sourced; the area is FVRD Electoral Area F ground with no civic centre, so Cascade Falls Regional Park was used as the measuring point.
Bus frequencies: not stated.

Durieu is an unincorporated farming settlement in the Hatzic Valley, not inside the City of Mission. The Fraser Valley Regional District (FVRD) lists Durieu among the historic settlement areas of Electoral Area F in the Hatzic Valley, with Hatzic Prairie, Miracle Valley and McConnell Creek

The valley floor runs between Hatzic Lake to the south and Stave Lake to the north, reached by Sylvester Road from the south and Stave Lake Road from the west, on streets including Durieu Road, Farms Road, Sward Road and Seux Road

Almost all Durieu homes are single detached houses and farm dwellings on acreages, because most inhabited valley land is farmland. The FVRD states the majority of the inhabited Hatzic Valley is in the Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR), with commercial and hobby farming alongside sparse residential use

FVRD rules, not City of Mission bylaws, govern building and zoning in Durieu, under the Official Community Plan for Hatzic Valley, Electoral Area F, Bylaw No. 0999, 2010, and FVRD Zoning Bylaw No. 1638, 2021

A secondary suite in Electoral Area F must sit inside the main house, not in a separate building. The FVRD records suites as freely permitted in Area F but only within the principal dwelling, not as a detached garden suite

On ALR land the Agricultural Land Commission (ALC) allows one principal residence up to 500 square metres plus one additional residence of 90 square metres on parcels up to 40 hectares, or 186 square metres above 40 hectares

blocks.text: Durieu: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Cascade Falls Regional Park, an FVRD regional park in the Hatzic Valley northeast of Durieu, is the valley's named day-use park, listed in the FVRD parks snapshot
Davis Lake Provincial Park sits at the north end of the valley off Sylvester Road and is listed by the FVRD among provincial parks in the regional district
School District No. 75 assigns middle school by elementary catchment: Deroche, Dewdney, Hatzic and Stave Falls elementary catchments all feed Hatzic Middle School under district policy

Fill placed on ALR land in Area F needs Agricultural Land Commission approval, and FVRD staff reports for Stave Lake Road and Dale Road parcels in Area F show fill applications being refused forwarding to the ALC
Durieu owners pay property tax to the Province, not to a city, because Durieu is a rural area. The Province states rural owners get their tax notice from the Surveyor of Taxes Office

There is no confirmed scheduled bus service in Durieu itself; the road link is Sylvester Road south to Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) and Stave Lake Road west into Mission, as the FVRD describes valley access
BC Transit and the FVRD consulted in April–May 2025 on a proposed new Highway 7 bus between Mission and Agassiz, which would be the first fixed route along the corridor east of Mission if funded

Check the parcel in the Riparian Areas Development Permit Area before planning work near a creek, because FVRD staff reports state all properties in the Hatzic Valley Official Community Plan area sit in that permit area, with farm activities exempt from a permit
Check ALR status by parcel identifier number (PID) on the ALC maps, because most inhabited valley land is in the ALR and ALR status controls second homes and subdivision
